definitions.gloss: outer frame; outer border; outer framework
definitions.explanation: The outermost frame of a structure, such as a window, picture, table, or screen layout. In contrast with {内枠|うちわく} (inner frame), {外枠|そとわく} encloses the whole object on the outside. Also used figuratively for the outer limits or overall framework of a plan, budget, or rule.

examples.japanese: {外枠|そとわく}を{黒|くろ}くする。
{写真|しゃしん}の{外枠|そとわく}に{木|き}の{額|がく}をつけた。
examples.english: I put a wooden frame around the outside of the photo.

examples.japanese: {窓|まど}の{外枠|そとわく}がさびてきたので{塗|ぬ}り{直|なお}す{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: The window's outer frame has started to rust, so we need to repaint it.

examples.japanese: {予算|よさん}の{外枠|そとわく}は{決|き}まったので、{次|つぎ}は{内訳|うちわけ}を{話|はな}し{合|あ}いましょう。
examples.english: The overall outline of the budget has been decided, so next let's discuss the breakdown.

notes:
Composed of {外|そと} (outside) and {枠|わく} (frame). A straightforward compound that can refer literally to the outer border of a physical object, or figuratively to the outer boundary or overarching shape of something abstract such as a plan or rule.

USAGE:
Common in concrete contexts — construction, carpentry, framing, furniture, screen design, and graphic layout. In business contexts, {外枠|そとわく}を{決|き}める means to fix the overall framework or limits of a project before filling in the details. In horse racing and other sports that use lane numbering, {外枠|そとわく} refers to the outside post position.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外枠|そとわく}を{つける}: to attach an outer frame
- {外枠|そとわく}を{囲|かこ}む: to enclose with an outer frame
- {外枠|そとわく}の{色|いろ}: color of the outer frame
- {予算|よさん}の{外枠|そとわく}: overall / outer limit of the budget
- {外枠|そとわく}だけ{決|き}める: to decide only the overall framework
- {外枠|そとわく}{発走|はっそう}: start from the outside post (horse racing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {内枠|うちわく}: inner frame — the opposite of {外枠|そとわく}; the frame on the inner side
- {枠|わく}: frame — the general word, without specifying inner or outside
- {枠組|わくぐ}み: framework — often used figuratively for the structure of a plan or system
- {縁|ふち}: edge; rim — the outer edge of an object, less structural than {枠|わく}
- {輪郭|りんかく}: outline; contour — the general shape of something seen from outside, not a physical frame
